title: Why The Market Is Crashing Right Now
creator: Asymmetric Investing
summary: Travis Hoy of Asymmetric Investing explains Thursday's sharp sell-off, arguing the market fears the AI buildout is slowing. Semiconductors and equipment led the fall as investors price in fewer data centres, lower chip demand, margin compression and multiple compression; even Palantir fell despite strong results. He works through Nvidia as the key example: it looks cheap at ~23x trailing earnings, but that multiple sits on record 75% gross and 65% operating margins, versus historical norms near 50-60% gross and 15-20% operating, so at normalised margins the P/E would be ~65-70, and Nvidia has periodically posted negative revenue growth since 2010. He questions AI demand beyond coding: Apple reportedly cut daily AI spend limits, Anthropic's Muse app is fading, Uber disclosed only ~500 AI-agent food orders and four rides, and Micron paused work on a $4.5bn Taiwan plant over a labour dispute. He stresses the election is not the driver, since both sides would have pushed back on AI costs for consumers. Healthcare (Eli Lilly, Johnson & Johnson), consumer staples, insurance and oil and gas held up. His own approach is pre-researched watchlists and programmatic buying: he adds opportunistically on drops and doubles his monthly Asymmetric Portfolio contribution if the S&P 500 or Nasdaq falls 20%, adding more at 30%. No explicit buy, hold or sell call is made on any single ticker. Caption garbles: 'Palanteer', 'Eli Liy', 'tranium' for Trainium.
